hypothesis: IPC columnar layout for large fact tables (P2)
blocking_question: Does any Atlas record family reach a volume where a columnar section beats row records, and is any Arrow mechanism needed beyond the generic columnar idea? (recorded as sequencing-blocked until a section writer existed -- it has since G64)

measurement.container: the real census container of cf706daea4: 3,444,275 bytes; STRING_TABLE 1,715,575 bytes / 37,769 strings; SEMANTIC_RECORDS (census facts) 1,628,507 bytes / 15,155 records; OBLIGATIONS 97,614 bytes / 1,683 records
measurement.family_volumes: census totals: 15,155 facts, 1,683 obligations, 81,080 typed records (the largest family is not stored in the container at all), 113,088 graph edges
measurement.row_layout: a fact is 107.5 bytes: an 8-byte record header plus 10 fields, each an 8-byte header (u16 tag, u8 wire, u8 flags, u32 length) around a 2-3 byte string-index varint; payload is 20% of the section (324,163 bytes), framing 80%
measurement.columnar_layout: one column per tag (a presence bitmap for optional tags, then the concatenated varints): facts 326,058 bytes (5.0x smaller raw), obligations 16,830 (5.8x)
measurement.after_compression: facts: row zlib-9 211,757 / xz 156,276 vs columnar zlib-9 150,525 / xz 107,828 -- 1.4x; obligations: row 4,820 / 1,352 vs columnar 505 / 508
measurement.consumer: none: the container is a gitignored local cache, never committed or transmitted

arrow_mechanisms.dictionary_encoding: already present: the sorted, deduplicated string table is the dictionary every string field indexes
arrow_mechanisms.validity_bitmaps: 2 of 10 fact fields are optional; a bitmap is the generic columnar idea, not Arrow-specific
arrow_mechanisms.ipc_framing_and_flatbuffers_metadata: duplicates the wire contract's own header, directory and schema identity (flatbuffers #22 G86 covered schema evolution)
arrow_mechanisms.record_batches_and_alignment: serve zero-copy vectorized compute, which no Atlas reader performs (rkyv #21 G85: the cache loads in ~0.35 s)

REFERENCE_ONLY: columnar format, dictionary/validity/offset buffers, IPC stream and file formats, record batches, compute kernels
